name: Multivariate Analysis Best Practices
description: This module captures the best practices for multivariate analysis, distilled from common failure modes and what tends to hold up over time.
content:
This module captures the best practices for multivariate analysis, distilled from common failure modes and what tends to hold up over time.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. Measure before optimizing any multivariate analysis bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.
2. Prefer explicit, readable multivariate analysis solutions over clever ones that are hard to verify.
3. When multivariate analysis decisions are ambiguous, favor the option that is easiest to reverse or extend later.
4. Surface known limitations of a chosen multivariate analysis approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.
5. When multivariate analysis guidance conflicts with a specific user instruction, defer to the user's explicit instruction and note the conflict.
6. Prefer the simplest multivariate analysis approach that satisfies the requirement over a more general one that isn't needed yet.
7. Check that multivariate analysis terminology is used consistently throughout, matching existing conventions in the surrounding context.
8. Document any non-obvious multivariate analysis decision with a short rationale so future readers understand the 'why', not just the 'what'.
9. Re-check edge cases relevant to multivariate analysis (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.
10. Keep multivariate analysis outputs reproducible: fix seeds, record versions, and avoid hidden non-determinism where it matters.
11. Validate multivariate analysis outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.
12. Keep multivariate analysis changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Avoid mixing unrelated multivariate analysis concerns into a single change; keep each change focused.
- Do not treat a single passing example as full verification of multivariate analysis correctness.
- Do not skip documenting multivariate analysis assumptions just because they seem obvious in the moment.

CLOSING NOTE
Revisit these multivariate analysis guidelines if the task's constraints change significantly during the work.
